# FAB

Figma: [02d. FAB](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-892) · Family: 02 Actions · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-05-20

A floating action button that anchors the most important action of a view to the bottom-trailing corner, hovering above scroll content with elevation. Available in Standard (circular) and Extended (pill with label) shapes.

Reference image (every variant, labelled): `knowledge/examples/components/fab/reference.png`

### FAB / Standard

A circular floating action button anchored to the bottom-trailing corner, above scroll content, holding the one most important action of a view as an icon.

Level: organism

Use when:
- A persistent jump back to the deals feed or a new-investment entry on a long scrolling screen: Variant=primary, Size=default
- A quiet persistent help or support entry point: Variant=secondary

Don't use when:
- The action needs a word to be understood (first-time users, unfamiliar action): use FAB / Extended
- A screen needs more than one persistent action: use IconButton or a FAB speed-dial
- The main action belongs in the page or sheet footer (Invest, Confirm): use Button
- Cancelling an investment on a primary surface: keep destructive actions inside a Dialog with Button Variant=destructive

Accessibility: Never ship Size=small as the only touch action on mobile (40dp fails the target size) and give the icon-only FAB a semantic label.

| Property in Figma | Code name | Type | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Icon | `icon` | instance swap | default Button Icon Placeholder | 398:2 |
| Variant | `variant` | variant | primary, secondary, destructive | primary |
| Size | `size` | variant | small, default, large | small |
| State | `state` | variant | default, hover, pressed, focused, disabled | default |

### FAB / Extended

A pill-shaped floating action button with a leading icon and a label, used when the single floating screen action needs words to be clear.

Level: organism

Use when:
- A labelled new-investment action on the portfolio screen, for example «استثمار جديد»
- First-time or unfamiliar actions where an icon alone would be ambiguous

Don't use when:
- The icon alone is universally clear: use FAB / Standard
- Support or chat entry points that should not compete with the main action: use FAB / Standard with Variant=secondary
- The action belongs in a form or sheet footer: use Button

Accessibility: One FAB per view at most, and keep the label short so it does not cover content near the bottom-trailing corner.

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

FAB stands for Floating Action Button - a Material Design pattern that originated on Android and is now standard across most modern mobile UIs. A FAB floats above the scrolling content of a view, anchored to the bottom-trailing corner, and represents the single most important action on that view.

Use FAB sparingly. A view should never have more than one FAB. If a screen needs more than one persistent action, reach for IconButton or an action bar instead - multiple FABs compete for attention and dilute the meaning of "primary action".

### At a glance

### Anatomy

FAB has two structural shapes that share a single API surface. Both follow Material 3 geometry: circular for Standard, pill-shaped for Extended. Below: live instances showing the slot composition.

Standard FAB

Container + centered icon

Extended FAB

Container + leading icon + label

| Container Circular (Standard) or pill (Extended). Holds the fill, shadow, and rounded shape. | Icon Centered (Standard) or leading (Extended). Instance swap - bring your own icon and color. | Label Extended only. Trailing in LTR, leading in RTL. Bound to text/* tokens by variant. | Shadow Effect style: Shadow/sm/md/lg/none. Reacts to state on primary + destructive. Secondary stays flat. |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

### Variants

FAB ships in three variants. Each card below shows the live variant with its semantic intent and usage rule.

Primary

Filled bg/brand/primary, drop shadow

The screen's single most important action. Default choice when in doubt. Use for "New deal", "Browse", "Compose", "Start investment".

Secondary

Filled bg/brand/primary-subtle, NO shadow

Quieter alternative paired alongside a primary FAB elsewhere on the screen, or when the action is supportive rather than headline. Reduced visual weight.

Destructive

Filled bg/error, drop shadow

Actions that delete, cancel, or otherwise irreversibly remove user data. Confirm the destructive intent in a dialog before executing. Never use as default screen affordance.

### States

FAB exposes five states. Each state is signaled by both color and elevation (drop shadow). The elevation change communicates affordance through depth, supporting users in poor lighting and high-contrast modes. Below: live FABs in each state.

default

Shadow / md

Resting state. Ready to receive input.

hover

Shadow / lg

Cursor over the FAB (desktop). Visually lifts.

pressed

Shadow / sm

Tap acknowledged. Sinks slightly.

focused

Shadow / md + 2dp ring

Keyboard focus. Outset border/focus stroke.

disabled

Shadow / none

Inert. Reads as flat with muted bg/disabled fill.

### Direction - LTR and RTL

Standard FAB has no direction-aware layout - it's a centered icon in a circular container, identical in LTR and RTL.

Extended FAB inherits direction from its parent text widget. In LTR contexts, the icon sits leading (left), label trailing (right). In RTL contexts, auto-layout HORIZONTAL flips this automatically - icon trailing (right), label leading (left). No separate RTL variant exists; the same component works for both directions at runtime.

LTR

Icon leads, label trails. Default reading order.

RTL

Icon trails, label leads. Auto-layout flips automatically at runtime.

إجراء

> **Info:** In Flutter, RTL flipping happens automatically via Directionality.of(context). In SwiftUI, set .environment(.layoutDirection, .rightToLeft) on the parent. Verify on the Account Statement screen - Arabic Extended FAB must read right-to-left.

### Icons

FAB exposes a single Icon property (instance swap). The placeholder shipped with the component is intentionally bland - at instance time, swap it for a Syntropy icon appropriate to the action.

"New deal"

Swap icon → add

"Edit"

Swap icon → edit

"Cancel investment"

Swap icon → close

> **Info:** The FAB does NOT override the icon's color. Whatever color the swapped icon brings, that's what shows. Syntropy icons declare their fill via icon/* semantic tokens - icon/on-brand for primary/destructive (white icon on filled), icon/brand/primary for secondary (brand-colored icon on subtle background).

> **Tip:** Icon sizes are fixed by FAB size: small and default use 24dp icons; large uses 36dp; Extended uses 24dp. Not currently bound to icon-size variables (no such tokens in the DS yet).

### Code examples

How to consume the FAB component in production code.

### Flutter

```dart
// Standard primary default
FloatingActionButton(
  onPressed: () => Navigator.pushNamed(context, '/new-deal'),
  child: Icon(SyntropyIcons.add),
  backgroundColor: SafqahColors.bgBrandPrimary,
)

// Extended primary
FloatingActionButton.extended(
  onPressed: _onTap,
  icon: Icon(SyntropyIcons.add),
  label: Text('New investment'),
  backgroundColor: SafqahColors.bgBrandPrimary,
)

// Small FAB - pair with a default-size primary
FloatingActionButton.small(
  onPressed: _onTap,
  child: Icon(SyntropyIcons.edit),
  backgroundColor: SafqahColors.bgBrandPrimarySubtle,
  foregroundColor: SafqahColors.iconBrandPrimary,
  elevation: 0,
  materialTapTargetSize: MaterialTapTargetSize.padded,
)
```

### React (token-driven)

```dart
<SafqahFAB
  variant="primary"
  size="default"
  icon={<SyntropyAdd />}
  onClick={handleNewDeal}
  ariaLabel="New deal"
/>

<SafqahFAB
  variant="primary"
  type="extended"
  icon={<SyntropyAdd />}
  label="New investment"
  onClick={handleNewInvestment}
/>
```

### Usage - Do and Don't

Concrete Safqah scenarios paired with their wrong counterparts. Each card includes a live FAB instance showing exactly what the right and wrong version looks like.

- **Do** · Home feed - Browse all deals: A persistent primary FAB anchored to the bottom-trailing corner. Always reachable so the user can jump back to the deals feed.
- **Don't** · Home feed - Browse all deals: Don't use secondary FAB for the screen's most important action - it reads as supportive, not primary. Reserve secondary for paired or alternative actions.
- **Do** · Portfolio - New investment: Extended FAB labels the action explicitly. Good for first-time users who need verbal context, especially in the portfolio screen where the action is unfamiliar.
- **Don't** · Portfolio - New investment: Don't use small (40dp) FAB as the only primary action on mobile - it fails the 44dp WCAG touch target minimum and is hard to tap.
- **Do** · Destructive - Cancel investment: Destructive FAB inside a confirmation dialog. Reserved for irreversible actions. Always pair with a clear "Are you sure?" prompt before invoking.
- **Don't** · Destructive - Cancel investment: Don't use destructive FAB as the default screen affordance. It belongs only inside confirmation flows, never on a primary surface where the user might tap it casually.
- **Do** · Help / Chat support: Secondary FAB for persistent chat or help entry points. Quieter visual weight so it doesn't compete with primary actions, but still always reachable.
- **Don't** · Help / Chat support: Don't use primary Extended FAB for support - it competes with the screen's actual primary action and dilutes "this is the most important thing".

### Notes from the maintainer

Implementation decisions, trade-offs, and things to watch out for.

> **Info:** FAB has no loading state. If you need to indicate async work after a tap (e.g. "Save draft" syncing), use a separate progress indicator overlay or a Snackbar/Toast confirmation rather than mutating the FAB itself.

> **Warning:** Small FAB (40dp) fails WCAG 2.5.5 - flag every use of it for review. It belongs in dense desktop or as a secondary action paired with a default-size primary, never as the sole touch target on mobile.

> **Tip:** When migrating from v1 Safqah components: v1 had no FAB component. Any "primary action button anchored to bottom-trailing" that exists in current Flutter screens was probably hand-rolled. Update those uses to import the new FAB component.

> **Info:** Material 3 spec defines large FAB radius as 28dp. We use 32dp because the closest primitive available is Radius/32 (Radius/24 would be too tight). A 4dp difference on a 96dp container is barely perceptible. If pixel-perfect M3 conformance becomes a requirement, add a Radius/28 primitive variable.

> **Info:** Material 3 specifies asymmetric horizontal padding for Extended FAB (16dp icon side, 24dp label side). We use symmetric 20dp on both sides so RTL flipping works automatically via auto-layout HORIZONTAL inversion. Acceptable trade-off but worth knowing.

> **Warning:** FAB places shadow via Effect Styles (Shadow/sm/md/lg/none), NOT bound to variables. Changing them requires editing the effect style, not a variable. Treat with care - a shadow style change cascades to everything using it.
